name: Google (Gmail)
summary: Creating the OAuth client takes minutes, but Gmail read scopes are classed as restricted. Going live for the public needs Google's OAuth verification plus an annual third-party security assessment (CASA). Budget weeks, and money for the assessor (the cost is not confirmed).

difficulty.label: Hard
difficulty.why: Restricted scopes need verification, a demo video, scope justification and an annual independent security assessment.

time.handsOn: Setup 30 min. Verification prep 2-5 days (demo video, privacy policy, scope justification, security remediation).
time.wait: Google says restricted scope verification can potentially take several weeks.

approval.type: OAuth app verification + CASA security assessment
approval.detail: Annual reverification at least every 12 months from the Letter of Assessment approval date. Exceptions exist for personal use, internal use, or service-owned data only.

agentCan: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes. For example, gmail.send and gmail.metadata sit in different categories than gmail.readonly, so a narrower design can avoid restricted status (check the scope's category in Cloud Console)
Draft the scope justification, privacy policy sections and data-deletion process that verification asks for
Write the demo-video script showing the consent screen and each scope in use
Verify endpoints, PKCE support and grant types from live discovery metadata
youMustDo: Create the Cloud project and consent screen in Google Cloud Console (needs your Google login and, for production, an app domain you can verify)
Record and submit the demo video, and answer Google's review emails
Engage an approved assessor, pay them, and fix the findings
Keep Owner/Editor and support contacts current so renewal notices reach someone

steps.title: Pick scopes with verification in mind
steps.detail: Google labels each scope non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted when you add it in the console. Restricted scopes trigger the security assessment if data reaches a third-party server. Reducing to sensitive-only scopes can cut weeks.

steps.title: Create a Cloud project, consent screen and OAuth client
steps.detail: Create the project, configure the consent screen, then create an OAuth client ID with your redirect URIs. Console: console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials (requires sign-in).

steps.title: Build and test while in Testing status
steps.detail: While unverified you can use test users only. From memory (not verified here): up to 100 test users, and refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing, which surprises teams who think their integration broke.

steps.title: Prepare the verification package
steps.detail: Required per Google: a demonstration video and a justification for each restricted scope. Also a privacy policy and a verified domain. Brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days, with an automated review usually done in minutes.

steps.title: Submit for OAuth verification
steps.detail: Respond to Google's emails promptly. Unanswered reviews stall.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: An independent assessor approved by Google checks that you handle data securely and can delete data on request. Google uses the App Defense Alliance CASA framework. The outcome is a Letter of Assessment (LOA).

steps.title: Plan annual reverification
steps.detail: Reverify at least every 12 months after your LOA approval date. Adding a restricted scope may require reassessment. Google emails when due.

requirements: Google Cloud project with the Gmail API enabled
Public privacy policy and app homepage on a domain you can verify
Independent security assessment if you use restricted scopes and store data on a server

gotchas.detail: Reading mail bodies is the typical trigger for CASA. A design that only sends mail or reads metadata may sit in a lighter category.

gotchas.issue: Several weeks is Google's own wording
gotchas.detail: 'The restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.' No upper bound is given.
Assessments are done by paid third-party labs. I could not confirm current prices, so get quotes early.
Personal use, internal use (e.g. Workspace internal app), or service-owned data may skip verification.
Recalled, not verified in this run.

blockers.fix: Expected until verification completes. Keep to test users, or move to production and complete verification.
Remove scopes you do not demonstrably use, or show their use in the video.
Re-architect to avoid storing restricted data on your server, or choose narrower scopes.

sources.title: Google: Restricted scope verification
sources.note: Fetched 2026-11-06. Source for CASA, annual reverification, several-weeks wording, brand verification time, exceptions, video and justification.

sources.note: The 100-test-user cap and 7-day refresh-token expiry are from prior knowledge and were NOT confirmed this run.

sources.title: Probe: Cloud Console credentials page
sources.note: Resolves but redirects to Google sign-in.

tested.result: Both 200. Endpoints: /o/oauth2/v2/auth and oauth2.googleapis.com/token. PKCE: plain, S256. Grants: authorization_code, refresh_token, device_code, jwt-bearer.
Redirects to sign-in, so project creation can't be done by an agent without the user's session.

confidence: High on the verification and CASA requirement (primary doc). Low on Testing-mode limits and assessor cost.
